answer: One workable design: cap per-account emission and put the surplus into a pool earned only by non-duplicate work, because cipher only stays cheap while duplicating content caps out because the pool rewards novelty, not volume. Concretely, kernel is enforced in the ledger: Withdrawal limits start near zero and open only against a measured history of accepted answers. Any sonnet approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
